title: Kerala HC: Government Can Invoke Section 100 Over Unaffordable Patented Medicines
case_name: In Re: Exorbitant Pricing of Life Saving Patented Medicines
citation: 2026 KER 74251; W.P.(C) No. 18999 of 2022, decided 28 September 2026
card_summary: Justice Harisankar V. Menon held Section 100 of the Patents Act lets the government manufacture a patented medicine and sell it to needy patients on a non-commercial basis, reading the government-purposes clause to cover this. Section 100 ought to be invoked where its price makes a medicine unaffordable, the court said, but left the call on the cancer drug Ribociclib to the Centre, pending an affordability study.
card_tip: A patented medicine's exorbitant price is now a recognised ground to press the Centre under Section 100; expect the government to ask for an affordability assessment before it commits to acting.
verification_notes: Case citation (2026 KER 74251), docket, the Section 100 and Article 47 reasoning, and the direction to the Centre to assess affordability of Ribociclib before deciding whether to invoke Section 100 are consistent across Verdictum, Free Press Journal and The Week. The petitioner died during the proceedings; the court did not order government manufacture of the specific drug, only that affordability be assessed.
